sections.text: Both packs are exploratory: addendum 2 lists Run A's pack among its exploratory outputs, and addendum 3 calls the B2 pack exploratory. No result here changes a registered verdict (E5 v2: supported H1, H2; B1: not supported; B2: Capability reached, clock not credited). This plan fixes the analysis before any rating exists, so that nobody can choose the analysis after seeing which one gives the nicer result. In the B2 pack, S* is the clock recipe and S*_b0 the same melody guide without the clock.

Anyone may rate who has not heard the labelled demo clips of either result package, has not seen either key, has not read the per-clip results of either run (results/gpu_run2/ and results/gpu_run3/, which give transcripts and scores by condition and recipe), and has not opened the first Run A pack or run experiments/run_all.py (see custody). Each rater confirms these four points in one line when handing in a sheet; a 'no', or no confirmation by closing, excludes the rater. The owner may rate; the agents do not. Each rater fills in a copy of the pack's ratings.csv named ratings_<nickname>.csv, is named by the file, and is told that the nickname and the counts will be public. One sheet per rater: if a rater hands in more than one, the last one before closing counts and the others are kept but not used. A sheet in another format (xlsx, et, numbers) is saved as CSV without changing any cell; both files are kept and hashed.

Ratings close when the owner says no more sheets are coming, and at the latest on 2026-11-30 at 23:59 UTC. The agents, who have seen the B2 key, take no part in deciding when to close, and nobody tallies any answer before closing. At closing the agents run analyze_ratings.py check on every sheet (it reads the pack's own blank ratings.csv and no key) and resolve every stop it reports by asking the rater through the owner; the reply goes into a copy of the sheet, both files are kept, and the change is reported. They then write exclusions.json (name, reason, date), the list of sheets with their arrival dates and sha256, and the owner's nickname, and commit these to the public repository before any key is opened. The key is opened once, after that commit; analyze_ratings.py is not run again with a real key until then, and no sheet is changed after the key is opened. A sheet that arrives after closing enters no test or label; it is listed with its arrival date only.

Answers are compared after Unicode normalisation (full-width letters count as ordinary ones), ignoring capital letters, spaces and a final full stop, exclamation mark or tilde. B2: A (also a段, 第一个, 第一段, 前者), B (b段, 第二个, 第二段, 后者), same (一样, 都一样, 一样好, 差不多, 都差不多, 相同, 没区别, 没有区别, 都好, 都对, 都清楚, both, equal, no difference), neither (都不, 都不行, 都不好, 两个都不行, 两个都不好, 两个都不, 都不对, 都不清楚, 都听不清, none); 不确定, 不知道, 说不清, ?, unsure and not sure count as no answer. Run A: yes (y, 是, 是的, 有, 有的, 能, 对, 可以, √, 听得清, 能听清, 重复, 有重复, 有伴奏), no (n, 否, 不是, 没有, 没, 无, 不, 不能, 不对, 不可以, ×, 听不清, 不重复, 没重复, 没有伴奏), unsure (not sure, ?, 不确定, 不太确定, 不知道, 说不清, 不好说); 不清楚 is not listed because it can mean either 'not clear' or 'I don't know'. An empty cell counts as no answer. Any other answer is unreadable: it counts as no answer, and every unreadable string is reported with its count. Sheets may be UTF-8, UTF-16 or GB18030, separated by commas, semicolons or tabs, with any line ending. Pair and clip names are read without case, spaces or leading zeros ('Pair 1' is pair_01). These stop the analysis until resolved at closing: a pair or clip name that is not in the pack, a name given twice with different answers, a row with answers but no name, a missing question column, two sheets for one nickname, and two byte-identical sheets under different nicknames (unless the owner confirms they come from two people). A sheet with no readable answer is left out and listed.

In plain words: on each pair we count the listeners who picked the clip with the clock and subtract those who picked the clip without it. Which recipe became clip A was a coin toss per pair. If the clock made no difference, every listener would have given the same answers whatever the coin tosses were, so the p value is the share of possible coin tosses that give a result at least as far from 'no difference' as the real one. The test is taken over the coin tosses that put the clock on side A as many times as the real key does (m of 24), each equally likely, and it compares how often listeners picked A when the clock was on A with how often they picked A when the clock was on B, so a listener who simply prefers clip A, or clip B, cannot move it. Exactly: with a_p the A answers minus the B answers on pair p and s_p = +1 when S* is on side A, the margin is D = sum_p s_p a_p and the centred margin is Dc = D - (2m - 24) mean_p(a_p), which is 2m(24 - m)/24 times (the mean of a_p where S* is on A minus the mean of a_p where S* is on B). The two-sided p is the share of side vectors with m entries +1 whose centred margin is at least as far from zero as the real one. The p of D over all 2^24 coin tosses is stored in the output for reference and sets no label. Labels, per question: 'listeners favour the clock' if Dc > 0 and p < 0.05, 'listeners favour no clock' if Dc < 0 and p < 0.05, otherwise 'no clear preference'. The two questions are reported separately, each with its own two-sided p; there is no correction for two questions, because the pack is exploratory.

Per question: D, Dc and m; the number of answers for S*, for S*_b0, same, neither, no answer and unreadable; the balanced share for S*, the mean of P(A | S* on A) and P(B | S* on B) over A and B answers, which is the share quoted in the write-up (the plain share for S* among A and B answers is also stored); the share of A among A and B answers, whatever the recipe (position preference); the number of pairs with a net vote each way; each rater's counts; and agreement with the machine scores on the same clips (results/gpu_run3/b2_result.json): for 'words clear', the share of A and B answers that picked the clip with more words recognised by Whisper, and by the CTC recogniser; for 'melody right', the share that picked the clip with more notes right on the separated vocal. Machine ties are left out. The side balance of the key and every other fact the agents' audit of the key found stay sealed until the ratings close, and are reported with them.

A listener can hear the context before the gap (A B A, A B C, or nothing for null), so these clips are blind to their labels but not to their condition. For each E5 condition and each E6 set (12 E4 lines, 8 extra verses, and both together): the yes rate of each question, yes / (yes + no); the gap question is reported for E5 clips only. 'The gap repeats an earlier phrase' for lit against ctl, a listener check related to H2 (it counts a repeat of any unit heard before the gap, while H2 counts only B against its altered copy B~): each clip's yes rate over raters, the mean over lit clips minus the mean over ctl clips, and an exact two-sided permutation test over every way to relabel the lit and ctl clips that have at least one yes or no answer (252 when all 10 do; the smallest possible p is then 2/252). Label: 'listeners hear more repeats after lit' if the difference > 0 and p < 0.05, 'fewer' if < 0 and p < 0.05, otherwise 'no clear difference'. The test runs on all raters, which is the headline result, and again without the owner's sheet; both are reported, and a difference that holds only with the owner's sheet is described as such (the analysis is run with --owner set to the owner's nickname, or 'none' if the owner did not rate). Agreement with the pitch tracker: a clip's listener majority (yes or no; ties left out) against whether the registered per-draw choice in results/gpu_run2/e5v2_main.json names a unit heard before the gap (lit: A, B; ctl: A, B, C; rel+2, rel+5, rel-3: A, B and A moved by the same step, that is T+2A, T+5A, T-3A; seq: A, T+2A, T+4A; ana: A, T+5A, B; null: no unit, since nothing plays before the gap). Any other choice counts as not heard before, including 'none', D (which plays after the gap) and B~; draws whose choice is 'tie' are left out. Reported as counts and Cohen's kappa (agreement beyond chance: 0 is chance, 1 is full agreement), with lit, ctl and null as the primary set, and again with moved copies of heard units also counted as heard (rel+k: T+kB; seq: T+6A; ana: T+5B). E6 clips: the majority for 'anyone singing' against E6's automatic singing check (the vocal gate), and for 'words intelligible' against Whisper recognising at least half the words (results/gpu_run2/e6_readout.json).

The first Run A pack's clip names followed a seed in the public code (experiments/run_all.py), so anyone could rebuild its key. On 2026-10-30, before any rating, the same 60 clips were renamed in an order from the operating system's random source (pack v2, entries in name order with fixed time stamps); the first pack is never handed to raters. The v2 clips are the same audio as the first pack's, so someone holding the first pack and the public code could still match them; that is why raters must not have opened the first pack or run the code. The B2 sides came from the operating system's random source when Run B packaged its clips. A plain sha256 of the B2 key could be reversed by trying all 2^24 side patterns, so each key's published fingerprint is sha256 of the salt file's 64 ASCII hex characters (no newline) followed by the key file's bytes. The salts are kept with the keys at the paths and commits in packs, and published with them. The agents opened both keys before writing this plan: the B2 key to audit the pack after Run B (pair order, that every clip matches its run, and that nothing in the files shows a side), the Run A key to read which experiments and conditions it holds and to rename the clips. They also ran the analysis on each real key with a sheet that answers 'same' or 'unsure' everywhere, last with the code registered here, to check it, and deleted those outputs. No rating existed then. Facts from the audit, the side balance among them, appeared in the agents' working output, which the owner can open. The B2 test does not depend on a rater not knowing the side balance: knowing it says nothing about which pairs have the clock on side A, and the centred margin cancels any preference for one side. No output of analyze_ratings.py with a real key is shared before the keys are published, because each output holds the key's sha256.

The analysis writes results/listening/<pack>_ratings.json with the hashes of the code, the key, the exclusions file and every ratings file, the excluded ones included. README.md and LOG.md report the labels, D, Dc, m, the p values and the counts, computed from all raters left after exclusions (each rater's own counts are in the JSON file). The keys and their salts are published with the results. A change to this plan after this file is committed goes into a new file, which the write-up names.
